review:
I often hear people refer to Game Dev Story (Kairosoft) and Game Dev Tycoon (Greenheart Games) as the original games that led to a sub-genre of game and software development games. Perhaps they did but the culmination of those early efforts came with Mad Games Tycoon. 

One thing I never enjoyed about GD Story and Tycoon is how bad the RNG could get and the black box nature of the mechanics which made them feel unfair after a while. Mad Games Tycoon doesn't pull any of that over your eyes, you have a pretty solid idea of where you went wrong and what you can do to improve next time. Progression makes sense and whatever you unlock has a meaningful impact on your ability to manage, sell and make money off your games.

This game just clicked really well and did a great job selling the feeling of managing a game studio. Great fun if you are into management games, I give it 8.5/10.

Video oyun geliştirme fikri, oyuncular için her zaman büyüleyici bir alan olmuştur. Kendi stüdyonu kurmak, bir ekip toplamak, doğru teknolojilere yatırım yapmak, hit oyunlar üretmek ve sektörde devleşmek… Mad Games Tycoon, tam olarak bu hayali oynanabilir bir simülasyona dönüştürüyor. Hem yönetim simülasyonu sevenlere hem de oyun sektörünün perde arkasına ilgi duyanlara hitap eden yapım, ilk bakışta sade görünse de içine girdikçe oldukça derin bir deneyim sunuyor.

Llevo muchísimas horas en Mad Games Tycoon y, sinceramente, es uno de esos juegos que parecen simples al principio… pero cuando empiezas a entender cómo funciona todo, no puedes parar.

Lo mejor del juego es la profundidad: no es solo “hacer juegos y ya”. Puedes diseñar motores, investigar tecnologías, gestionar equipos, analizar el mercado, crear consolas, comprar compañías… y todo influye de verdad en el resultado. Cada decisión cuenta, y cuando un juego te sale perfecto, la satisfacción es brutal.

También me gusta mucho que no te regala nada. Tienes que aprender de tus errores, revisar informes, mirar tendencias y optimizar cada detalle. Esa curva de aprendizaje hace que cada partida sea distinta y que siempre quieras mejorar el siguiente proyecto.

A nivel de contenido, tiene muchísimo: campañas largas, modo libre, dificultad ajustable y una rejugabilidad enorme. Es el típico tycoon en el que dices “voy a hacer un juego más” y cuando miras el reloj han pasado horas.

Si te gustan los juegos de gestión o el mundo del desarrollo de videojuegos, este es prácticamente obligatorio. No será el más vistoso gráficamente, pero en jugabilidad y profundidad está a un nivel altísimo.

Totalmente recomendado.

Great and very addicting game that has a few issues.
I came into this game way late. I was going to get the second one but figured id try this one first cause it was cheaper.
Must say I was very impressed. I booted it up and next thing I knew it was 3 am and i was wondering where the day went.
It takes what game dev tycoon did and polishes it to a shine.
I especially like how the genre combos that work make sense. I always felt like in game dev tycoon you needed a guide to figure out what works with what. Here it just makes sense, including the sliders. Not knowing anything about the system you can get pretty darn close just knowing what people like in each genre.
I loved all the different ways you could play and make money but there was one thing i had an issue with...and its huge to me.
Time...
How fast the time goes by. I like to take my time and relax with a game like this. I dont want to feel on edge the whole time trying to do 50 things at once. Especially in the early game you will try to research all the new tech, then go and make or update your game engine if your lucky do a contract or a round of training, then go make a game and by the time you start making a game....the next tech is out and now you on an old engine. There were soooo many times Id want to start working on a game, but id have so many things coming at me so fast the next thing i know a year or two has gone by and i still haven't started my game. Even on the slowest setting.
For instance at the start i may want to train up my character, then work on an engine, then maybe make a game.
But i start training and by the time im done, two new tech upgrades have come. So I research them, then go make my engine, another new tech comes. So i start researching them but now I have a stack of contracts to do.
Its always something. 
Thats my biggest issue. I cant just sit back and relax and take my time.

Other than that...its a great game and I cant wait to try MGT 2, which ive heard is the much better version.
Hopefully that one will allow me to take my time, especially when you consider that once the in game tech dies out....there is no more after so many years and all the games you make get lower and lower scores after because its made with old tech...even though you have the best the game has...and nobody wants to rush to an end game that punishes you for making it to the end game...lol.

Overall...and easy B+ game.

[h1]Qu'est-ce que Mad Games Tycoon ?[/h1]
[quote=Peet]Mad Games Tycoon est un jeu de gestion développé par Eggcode, sorti en 2015. Il vous place à la tête d’un studio de jeux vidéo dans les années 80, avec pour mission de créer des jeux à succès, agrandir vos locaux, recruter des équipes, et devenir un acteur majeur de l’industrie. Un concept qui parlera à tous les amateurs de Game Dev Tycoon, avec ici une approche un poil plus complexe et plus “simulation poussée”.[/quote]

[h1]Un gameplay de gestion complet mais un peu austère[/h1]
Dès les premières minutes, on sent que Mad Games Tycoon veut aller plus loin que la concurrence en matière de profondeur. Il ne s’agit pas seulement de développer un jeu, mais de gérer toute une chaîne de production : la création du moteur, la location de locaux, la fabrication physique des copies, et même votre propre label d’édition si le cœur vous en dit.

Mais attention : cette richesse vient aussi avec son lot de prise de tête. L’interface, bien que fonctionnelle, n’est pas toujours très lisible. On se perd vite entre les menus, les bureaux à gérer, et les nombreuses options disponibles dès les premières heures. C’est un jeu qui demande du temps d’adaptation, mais qui devient très satisfaisant une fois qu’on a compris toutes les mécaniques.

[h1]Une direction artistique datée[/h1]
Graphiquement, le jeu fait le strict minimum. Ce n’est clairement pas pour ses visuels que vous y jouerez. On est sur un style cartoon très basique, presque “placeholder”, qui rend le jeu lisible mais pas vraiment attractif. L’important est ailleurs : dans les chiffres, les choix de stratégie, et la progression.

[h1]Des mécaniques intéressantes mais parfois déséquilibrées[/h1]
Il y a beaucoup à faire dans Mad Games Tycoon, et c’est là sa force. Entre la recherche de nouvelles technologies, les campagnes marketing, la fabrication de consoles, ou encore la gestion du personnel, on peut passer des heures à fignoler son empire vidéoludique.

Mais certaines mécaniques semblent sous-exploitées ou mal équilibrées : le système de notes des jeux, par exemple, paraît parfois injuste ou trop aléatoire. De plus, la rentabilité de certains projets n’a pas toujours de logique apparente, ce qui peut frustrer les amateurs de calculs optimisés.

[h1]Un vrai plaisir pour les fans du genre[/h1]
Malgré ses défauts, j’ai passé un excellent moment sur Mad Games Tycoon. C’est un jeu qui gratte une vraie envie de gestion précise et qui propose une montée en puissance gratifiante. On part d’un petit bureau miteux pour finir avec un studio géant qui enchaîne les blockbusters.

Ce n’est pas le plus accessible ni le plus joli, mais c’est un jeu de passionnés pour les passionnés. Et une fois qu’on est accroché, difficile de décrocher.

Mad Games Tycoon is a detailed and addictive game development simulator that laid the foundation for what would later become a more refined experience in its sequel. At its core, it offers a compelling premise: start a humble studio in the 1980s and grow it into an industry giant over the course of decades. Along the way, you'll develop custom engines, experiment with genre and topic combinations, hire and train staff, and eventually venture into publishing, console development, and large-scale operations.

Despite its relatively simple visual presentation, the game boasts surprising depth. The core gameplay loop (developing games, optimizing engines, expanding your office) remains satisfying throughout, and there’s a strategic layer to how you assign staff, manage genres, and anticipate platform trends. Players can mix genres and topics, tweak development sliders to match audience expectations, and license or sell their game engines for additional revenue. Over time, you unlock more advanced departments like QA, marketing, motion capture, or even console design, allowing your studio to diversify and scale.

What makes Mad Games Tycoon engaging is the sheer variety of interconnected systems. There’s a strong sense of progression, and each new playthrough offers fresh challenges depending on shifting trends and platform dynamics. While the systems are generally intuitive, the game still rewards experimentation and planning. The fake review quotes and humorous game name generator also give it a light-hearted personality that keeps things fun even during the grind.

That said, many of its systems have aged, particularly when viewed next to its sequel. For instance, there is no multiplayer mode, so competition is limited to AI studios, which eventually become predictable. Staff management is relatively shallow: employees have skill stats, but lack traits, personalities, or morale systems, and they’ll never resign no matter how badly they’re treated. Sequels exist, but there’s no IP tracking or franchise value system. Games, once released, are done, sicne there’s little to no post-launch support for MMOs or ongoing updates. Publishing is also simplistic: you sign a deal, and the game sells, with no physical production or logistics to manage.

The building system is limited to single-floor expansions within fixed office sizes, and performance can degrade in late-game studios with many rooms and employees. It becomes clear that while Mad Games Tycoon had big ambitions, it was restrained by the limitations of its engine and its time.

Still, credit where it’s due: this was (and still is) one of the most feature-rich indie game development sims when it came out. It successfully balances accessibility with simulation depth, and its replayability is enhanced by random trends, platform popularity shifts, and a large pool of game combinations.

In conclusion, Mad Games Tycoon remains a rewarding experience for fans of the genre, especially those looking for a more straightforward, single-player challenge. However, players discovering the series for the first time may want to start with Mad Games Tycoon 2, which meaningfully expands on nearly every system introduced here, offering deeper mechanics, improved simulation, and a more complete vision of what this series aspired to be.

Score: 7/10 – A strong and ambitious base that has since been surpassed, but still stands as an enjoyable and worthwhile tycoon sim.

There's quite an amount of detail and depth into not only developing games but also starting your own company and publishing your own games, moreso then it's obvious comparison Game Dev Tycoon. Although it is a bit trial and error at first figuring out which genre and attribute combinations work the best which can be a bit of a nuisance when you have limited money and resources at the start of the game.

Barely started the sequel atm but if they've taken the feedback from players about what works here and what could be improved then I'll say the second game would defiantly be the better option to buy. Having said that I would still recommend people give this one a try as a starting point.

Mad Games Tycoon bietet eine ansprechende Simulation für aufstrebende Spieleentwickler. Der Spieler übernimmt die Rolle eines Studioleiters, erstellt Spiele, entwickelt Mitarbeiter und steigt auf. Das Spiel bietet Tiefe mit zahlreichen anpassbaren Aspekten, von Spieleentwicklung bis zur Büroeinrichtung. Die Grafik ist einfach, aber funktional. Allerdings fehlt es an Vielfalt bei den Spielfeatures und einige Mechaniken sind repetitiv. Die steile Lernkurve könnte Neueinsteiger abschrecken, obwohl sie langfristige Herausforderungen bietet. Die anfängliche Motivation kann nach einiger Zeit nachlassen, wenn man sich auf denselben Ablauf einstellt. Die musikalische Untermalung ist unscheinbar. Insgesamt ist Mad Games Tycoon eine solide Management-Simulation für Spielefans, die bereit sind, sich mit den komplexen Aspekten der Spieleentwicklung auseinanderzusetzen, jedoch mit einigen Mängeln in der Langzeitmotivation.
